title: Aider repository map
finding: Aider builds a compact map of important classes, functions, types and call signatures so a coding model can select relevant source context without pasting the entire repository.
decision: ADAPT: map Kotlin source/import/test relationships and load only relevant slices; keep the first map explicitly static.

title: SWE-agent ACI
finding: The ACI uses syntax validation before edits, bounded file viewing, compact search results and explicit success output for empty commands. These interface choices improve engineering-agent reliability; they do not replace the brain.
decision: ADAPT: enforce patch checks and bounded observations; do not transplant the framework.

title: mini-SWE-agent architecture
finding: The current mini-SWE-agent project emphasizes a small agent loop, independent subprocess actions, linear trajectories and interchangeable local/container environments.
decision: ADAPT: keep the workbench dependency-light and make tasks/evidence replayable; avoid adding a large agent framework to the Android APK.

title: OpenHands Software Agent SDK architecture
finding: OpenHands separates agents, tools, conversations, events, workspace implementations and security policy; local and ephemeral workspaces are explicit alternatives.
decision: ADAPT: separate research assistant task/workspace/evidence from the brain and app runtime; use external Git worktrees for isolation.

title: SWE-bench evaluation guide
finding: SWE-bench applies candidate patches to real repositories and runs repository tests in repeatable isolated environments before grading resolution.
decision: ADAPT: require base commit, candidate diff, real test execution, immutable run evidence and independent acceptance criteria; use Git worktrees rather than Docker on the Poco.

title: Numeric gradient verifier coverage blind spot
finding: The numerical checker samples only coordinates whose analytic gradient magnitude exceeds 1e-8 and only requires at least one coordinate overall. A parameter group with all-zero analytic gradients could be skipped entirely without the test detecting missing backprop coverage. Current unit test checks one configuration and at most two coordinates per group.
decision: OPEN HYPOTHESIS brain-gradient-coverage-001: add deterministic zero/non-zero coordinate coverage per every parameter array, across seeds/head counts/context lengths, then run Gradle baseline/candidate. No brain code changed.

title: Stanford CS231n gradient checking guidance
finding: The lecture recommends centered finite differences, symmetric relative error with explicit both-zero handling, caution with float32 and epsilon, and checking a few coordinates in every separate parameter tensor rather than random sampling that can omit small groups.
decision: ADAPT as per-array deterministic coverage and precision-aware comparison; no source code copied.

title: PyTorch gradcheck mechanics
finding: PyTorch reconstructs analytic and numerical Jacobians and compares them using finite differences; its defaults target double precision and may not work reliably with lower-precision inputs.
decision: ADAPT central differences and explicit precision/tolerance calibration for KN-003 float32; do not copy framework code.

title: JAX directional gradient checks
finding: JAX checks gradients in a randomly chosen direction to make numerical checking affordable for larger parameter spaces.
decision: ADAPT a reproducible seeded directional-derivative cross-check per parameter array, in addition to coordinates, to reduce cost without omitting parameter groups.
